summary: This Wikipedia article describes the Salar de Atacama, the largest salt flat in Chile, located about 55 km south of San Pedro de Atacama. It covers the salt flat's size and surroundings, its geology and hydrology, and its role as a major source of lithium, including lithium production figures, extraction process, and tensions with the indigenous Likan Antay people over water use and benefits.
one_line: Overview of Salar de Atacama, Chile's largest salt flat, covering its geology, hydrology, and its importance as a lithium production hub.
key_facts: Salar de Atacama is located 55 km (34 mi) south of San Pedro de Atacama and is the largest salt flat in Chile.
The salt flat encompasses 3,000 km² (1,200 sq mi), about 100 km long and 80 km wide, making it the third largest in the world after Salar de Uyuni in Bolivia and Salinas Grandes in Argentina.
The average elevation of the salt flat is about 2,300 m above sea level.
Salar de Atacama is surrounded by mountains and lacks drainage outlets; to the east it is enclosed by the main chain of the Andes and to the west by the Cordillera de Domeyko.
Laguna Cejar is a sink hole lake in the Salar de Atacama, 18 km from San Pedro, with a salt concentration ranging from 5 to 28%.
The Salar de Atacama basin is bordered on the north by the Salado River basin, a sub-basin of the Loa River basin.
Its main tributaries are the San Pedro and Vilama rivers, which originate to the north of the salt flat.
Located in the Lithium Triangle, Salar de Atacama is the world's largest and purest active source of lithium, containing 27% of the world's lithium reserve base.
As of 2017, Salar de Atacama provided about 36% of the world's lithium carbonate supply, followed by China with 23%.
Atacama's brine has a lithium concentration of 2,700 parts per million, an evaporation rate of 3,500 mm per year, and under 30 mm average annual rainfall.
The Likan Antay people are the indigenous inhabitants of Salar de Atacama and its surrounding areas.
Chile signed the Indigenous and Tribal Peoples Convention, 1989 in 2008, under whose framework negotiations with lithium companies occur.
Sociedad Química y Minera (SQM) and Albemarle operate in Salar de Atacama and are among the largest lithium producers in the world.
The evaporation pond stage of lithium extraction usually takes 12 to 18 months to reach a lithium concentration of 6%.
Final processing is done at Planta Salar del Carmen and Planta La Negra near the city of Antofagasta on the coast.
